answer: Treat context 56 as two records, not one. "Context" in an excavation maps onto CRMarchaeo's A8 Stratigraphic Unit, and A8's own scope note ties an instance to a form that can be attributed to a single genesis event or process. A posthole cut (Trench 3) and a pit-fill deposit (Trench 7) are two different genesis events with different locations, so no honest single A8 instance can cover both, no matter what number is written on the sheet. The number clash is a separate, secondary problem: E42 Identifier's own scope note only promises uniqueness/permanence 'within the context of one or more organisations' -- that promise was broken here by two supervisors drawing from the same book without cross-checking, not by the archaeology. So: two A8 Stratigraphic Unit instances, each P1 is identified by / P48 has preferred identifier an E42 Identifier with the string '56'. Because A8's Required block (P157, P89, P196, P45, P53) never includes P1/P48, the model already treats the identifier as incidental documentation rather than what constitutes the entity's identity -- consistent with letting the string collide without collapsing the two features. If the digitisation project wants to record the mistake itself rather than silently renumbering one context, an E15 Identifier Assignment per context sheet (P14 carried out by the respective supervisor, P37 assigned the E42 '56', P141 assigned it to that A8 instance) documents who issued which '56' and when, which is exactly the kind of provenance-of-error E15 exists for.

rejected_alternatives.option: Single A8 Stratigraphic Unit record spanning both trenches (one 'context 56' that turns out to describe two features)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: A8's scope note requires the unit's form to be attributable to a single genesis event or process. A posthole cut and a pit-fill deposit are two different genesis events in two different trenches, so merging them into one instance misrepresents the stratigraphy regardless of the shared label.

rejected_alternatives.option: L54 is same as between the two context-56 records
rejected_alternatives.why_not: L54 asserts the two records co-refer to the same real-world entity. Nothing in the case supports that -- the sheets describe physically and stratigraphically distinct features that only collided on a number.
